text:
sam.w: incident-bot: PagerDuty page triggered PD-90172 for vectorizer-prod — 503 spike and ~50% jump in p50 after canary deploy v2.3.1
pd-bot: Auto-page: PD-90172 | Severity: P1 | Escalation policy: oncall-engineering | link: https://pd/ref/PD-90172
sam.w: Observed spike immediately post-deploy (12:02 UTC). Canary hosts in eu-west returning 5xx on /v1/vectorize. Rolling errors and some OOM traces reported.
maya.r: acked PD-90172 :raised_hand: I'm taking primary. Gathering container logs and host metrics.
oncall-eng: oncall-eng taking channel. Immediate action: divert canary traffic back to stable (v2.3.0) while we triage. Will run trafficctl.
alex.k: running:
```
./ops/trafficctl divert --service vectorizer-prod --from v2.3.1 --to v2.3.0 --pool canary
```
alex.k: trafficctl output:
```
INFO 12:04:02 starting diversion
INFO drained canary-01
INFO drained canary-02
INFO routing 100% canary -> stable
```
maya.r: logs from canary-02:
```
2026-09-03T12:03:07Z vectorizer ERROR handler failed: upstream returned 503, reason=kv-cache-miss, trace=0xabc123
2026-09-03T12:03:08Z kernel: [oom_kill] pid 8923 invoked oom_killer
```
lina.s: infra says canary containers hit OOMs (oom_kill). Kernel logs and dmesg snippets uploaded to infra:logs (private). Looks correlated with quantized inference path.
sam.w: initiating rollback command for canary:
`deploy rollback --service vectorizer-prod --version v2.3.0 --scope canary` — confirmed started at 12:06 UTC.
pd-bot: PD-90172 acknowledged by maya.r at 12:05 UTC. Escalations paused.
customer-success-bot: Heads up — 2 enterprise customers in EU reported errors via support (tickets #4238, #4241). CS alerted and engaged. @lina.s flagged for customer comms.
alex.k: attempted quick mitigation: toggled feature-flag to disable quant path on canary: `vectorizer.quant_path=false` — pushed to canary but since canary already rolled back, leaving flag change for canary staging.
maya.r: question — is the regress limited to quant kernels or an environment change? CPU/mem graphs show spike only when quant path is enabled.
lina.s: confirmed: memory footprint climbs ~3x on quant path leading to cgroup OOM under sustained concurrent requests. Likely regression introduced by upstream kernel/compiler or a quant change in v2.3.1.
oncall-eng: mitigation state: traffic diverted, canary drained, stable handling production traffic. Monitoring p50/p99 and 5xx. No broader customer impact now, but two customers routed to canary prior to diversion.
sam.w: short incident summary draft: suspected cause — quantized inference path change in v2.3.1 increasing memory usage and triggering OOMs under concurrency; impact — canary-only initially but leaked to a tiny fraction of customers; mitigation — traffic diversion + canary rollback + feature-flag to disable quant path; next steps — revert quant changes, add resource limits and e2e test for quant path, add early canary healthcheck for OOM pattern.
maya.r: prepping timeline & artifacts for postmortem; will upload collected logs and `trafficctl` transcript to #incidents-postmortems.
alex.k: verifying metrics: non-canary production 5xx back to baseline, canary pool drained.
lina.s: updated support tickets with mitigation notes and ETA for customer follow-up. CS will confirm customer recoveries before PD close.
oncall-eng: handing off to next oncall at 13:00 UTC — leaving notes and actions required in this thread.
sam.w: thanks — please keep PD open until CS confirms both customers recovered. pd-bot, leave PD on hold.
pd-bot: PD-90172 status: On hold (awaiting CS confirmation). Manual close required.
customer-success-bot: CS updated, will ping this thread when both tickets are resolved.
maya.r: taking final: all canary services are stable on v2.3.0, monitoring remains green. Handoff complete.

Notes: commands and logs above are redacted placeholders. Attachments uploaded to infra:logs and incidents:attachments for postmortem.
